chunks: As for what is in it from Shuʿayb ibn Wāqid concerning the prohibitions, I have narrated it from Ḥamzah ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Zayd ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon them. He said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Abharī narrated to me. He said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Zakariyyā al-Jawharī al-Ghallābī al-Baṣrī narrated to us. He said: Shuʿayb ibn Wāqid narrated to us. He said: al-Ḥusayn ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon them, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade eating while in a state of janabah, and said: it brings about poverty. And he mentioned the hadith in its full length as it appears in this book.

key_terms.الْأَكْلِ عَلَى الْجَنَابَةِ: eating while remaining in a state of janabah
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْفَقْرَ: poverty, mentioned here as a consequence
key_terms.الْمَنَاهِي: prohibitions or forbidden matters mentioned in hadith

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about eating in a state of janabah?
ai.summary: This report preserves the transmission chain for a hadith of prohibitions narrated through Shuʿayb ibn Wāqid. In the matn, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbids eating while in a state of janabah and states that it leads to poverty.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: And whatever is narrated from Shuayb ibn Waqid regarding the prohibitions, I have narrated it from Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Ṭalib, peace be upon them, who said: Abu Abdullah Abd Al-Aziz ibn Muhammad ibn ʿIsa Al-Abhari narrated to me, who said: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Zakariya Al-Jawhari Al-Ghallabi Al-Baṣri narrated to us, who said: Shuayb ibn Waqid narrated to us, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Al-Ṣadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Amir Al-Muʾminin Ali ibn Abi Ṭalib, peace be upon him, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, forbade eating while in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah) and said that it causes poverty, and he narrated the hadith in its entirety as recorded in this book.
